nodes.name: Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement:
Let $\nu \in \mathrm{int}(\mathcal M)$.  For any $\epsilon>0$, 
we can choose a neighborhoods $U$ of $(\nu,\infty)$  and 
$V$ of $\sigma_\nu$ in Theorem 4.3 
so that they also  satisfy the following: 
$V$ is contained in the domain $\Omega$ of the trace coordinate map, and 
 for any $(\mu,\zeta) \in U$ with $\zeta  \ne \infty$, we have 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|\mu-i\alpha| \le \epsilon$, and 
\item $|\zeta-4\pi i/\lambda(\beta)| \le \epsilon \, \mathrm{Im}\,\zeta$, 
\end{enumerate}
where $(\alpha,\beta)={\mathrm{Tr}}(\sigma_{\mu,\zeta})$ is the trace coordinates of $\sigma_{\mu,\zeta}$

nodes.name: Proposition 5.2
nodes.statement:
For any $\nu \in \mathrm{int}(\mathcal M)$, there exists $\epsilon_0>0$ which satisfy the following: 
For any $0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0$ and $I>0$, there exists $K>0$ such that 
for all $z \in \mathbb C$ with $|z|>K$ and $0<\mathrm{Im}\,z<I$, 
$
B_\epsilon(\nu,z) \subset \mathcal A
$
implies
$
B_{\epsilon/2}(\nu,z) \subset \mathcal D. 
$

nodes.name: Lemma 6.7
nodes.statement:
Under the same assumption as in Theorem  6.6, 
we have the following: 
For any $\alpha \in \mathrm{int}(i \mathcal M({2\xi}))$ 
there exists $\epsilon>0$  such that 
$B_\epsilon(\alpha) \subset  \mathrm{int}(\mathcal L(\beta_n))$
for all large $n$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.6
nodes.statement:
Let 
$\{\beta_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ be a sequence in $\mathbb C \setminus [-2,2]$ 
which converges to $2$ as $n \to \infty$. 
Suppose that 
$\lambda(\beta_n)$ converge tangentially to $0$. 
We further assume that there exists a complex number $\xi$ with $\mathrm{Im}\,\xi \ge 0$
and a sequence $m_n$ of integers  with $|m_n| \to \infty$ 
such that 
$$
\lim_{n \to \infty} \left(\frac{2\pi i}{\lambda(\beta_n)}-m_n\right)= \xi. 
$$
Then we have the following: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal L(\beta_n)$ converge to $i \mathcal M({2\xi})$ in the sense of Hausdorff as $n \to \infty$. 
\item $\mathrm{int}(\mathcal L(\beta_n))$ converge to $\mathrm{int}(i \mathcal M({2\xi}))$ in the sense of Carath\'{e}odory as $n \to \infty$. 
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proposition 5.3
nodes.statement:
For any $\nu \in \mathrm{int}(\mathcal M)$, there exists $\epsilon_0>0$ which satisfy the following: 
For any $0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0$ there is $I>0$ such that 
$
B_{\epsilon,I}(\nu) \subset \mathcal A
$
implies 
$
 B_{\epsilon/2,2I}(\nu)  \subset \mathcal D. 
$

nodes.name: Lemma 6.9
nodes.statement:
Under the same assumption as in Theorem 6.8, we have the following: 
For any $\alpha \in \mathrm{int}(i \mathcal M)$ there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that 
$B_\epsilon(\alpha) \subset  \mathrm{int}(\mathcal L(\beta_n))$
for all large $n$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.8
nodes.statement:
Let $\{\beta_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ be a sequence in $\mathbb C \setminus [-2,2]$ which converges to $2$ as $n \to \infty$. 
Suppose that $\lambda(\beta_n)$ converge horocyclically to $0$.  
Then we have the following: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal L(\beta_n)$ converge to $i\mathcal M$ in the sense of Hausdorff as $n \to \infty$. 
\item $\mathrm{int}(\mathcal L(\beta_n))$ converge to $\mathrm{int}(i \mathcal M)$ in the sense of Carath\'{e}odory as $n \to \infty$. 
\end{enumerate}
